label: Supplied vernacular Bhakti egalitarian critique of caste and gender orthodoxy
description: The anti-caste Bhakti traditions championed by figures like Mirabai and Kabir in western India gave nineteenth-century Satyashodhak thinkers, including Savitribai Phule, an indigenous moral vocabulary challenging Brahmanical exclusion.
dialecticalTension: Bridges devotional anti-caste spirituality with rationalist educational emancipation.
historicalContext: Bhakti egalitarian heritage invoked across 19th-century Maharashtrian social reform.

citations.author: Gail Omvedt
citations.work: Seeking Begumpura: The Social Vision of Anticaste Intellectuals
